issues.failure_explanation: The only proved layer estimate, Lemma lem:neumann-layer-correction, treats a homogeneous layer equation driven by outer-boundary conormal data. It does not establish existence or a polynomial estimate for a layer equation with arbitrary volume forcing F in H^{-1}_0. Extending a zero-entrance layer solution by zero also produces an interface conormal distribution whose required bound is not shown. Thus the asserted forced estimate for general F does not follow from the preceding lemmas.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a forced PML-layer lemma for arbitrary H^{-1}_0 volume data, including control of the entrance conormal trace created by zero extension, and then derive the global forced Robin estimate from that lemma.
issues.overall_effect: The polynomial exact-BIE inverse bounds and several perturbation estimates used in the Neumann-series analysis lack their stated stability input, so the computable-BIE convergence theorem is not established by the given proof.
issues.title: Forced PML stability is not established for general layer-supported sources
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial new layer-stability argument is required. It need not change the advertised convergence result if established, but it is more than a routine algebraic omission.

issues.failure_explanation: The nearest reflected kernel is removed from the remainder only after multiplication by χ_im(x)χ_im(y). The stated assumptions do not require χ_im to equal one in a neighborhood of the vertical-boundary endpoints. Wherever 1-χ_im(x)χ_im(y) is nonzero arbitrarily close to such an endpoint, E_sigma still contains a nearest reflection with s+s' arbitrarily small, whose Hankel kernel is only algebraically small rather than exponentially separated. Proposition prop:reflected-kernel-estimate therefore cannot supply the claimed exponential operator bound for E_sigma under the stated cutoff assumptions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require χ_im to be identically one on a fixed neighborhood of each relevant vertical-boundary endpoint and arrange its transition region at a fixed positive tangential distance from that endpoint; then verify that every term left in E_sigma has the required separation.
issues.overall_effect: The exponential smallness of the separated remainder, and hence both Neumann-series arguments that use it, are not justified for the cutoff as defined.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Both fields satisfy the homogeneous Neumann condition on the artificial boundary.

issues.failure_explanation: The flat model L_{sigma,t} assumes the vertical stretching coefficient is one and is posed on unbounded half-planes in n. In the actual domains, α_2 is nontrivial in the top and bottom PML regions, and the domains have finite horizontal artificial boundaries. Since η depends only on s, ηU_{sigma,t} extends into those vertical-PML regions and to the horizontal outer boundaries. Consequently L_sigma(ηU_{sigma,t}) has coefficient-mismatch residuals wherever α_2 differs from one, not only the commutator supported on supp η', and ηU_{sigma,t} need not satisfy the homogeneous Neumann condition on the horizontal artificial boundary. The displayed PDE for W_{sigma,b} therefore omits volume and boundary forcing terms.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include the vertical coefficient-mismatch and horizontal-boundary residuals in the correction problem and prove that their induced traces near Γ_im are sufficiently small, or replace the half-plane model by a localized model satisfying the full finite-domain coefficients and boundary conditions.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate comparing Q_sigma with its half-line model is unproved, so the smallness of the exact inverse applied to the nearest-image perturbation and the final computable-BIE solvability and convergence argument are unreliable.
issues.title: The cutoff flat model omits vertical-PML and outer-boundary residuals
issues.why_classification: Repair requires additional nontrivial residual estimates or a revised local comparison construction, but it may remain localized and need not alter the final convergence rate.
